description: DEPRECATED — prefer the `check` tool. Verifies one load-bearing conclusion against evidence references you supply and returns a signed ProofPacket receipt (status valid | invalidated | could_not_verify, receipt.decision ALLOW | REVIEW | BLOCK). Kept only for existing pilot integrations that pass explicit evidence_refs; it will be removed. New calls should use `check`, which needs no evidence list, is answered from watched state with no model call and no fetch, and keeps monitoring the facts afterwards.

as_of.description: RFC 3339 cutoff for what the conclusion may rely on

conclusion.description: the exact assertable proposition the downstream workflow intends to rely on — a STATEMENT of what you believe, in the indicative. The API rejects anything phrased as a request or a question, INCLUDING the phrasing this tool's name invites: 'verify whether/if/that …', 'check whether …', 'is X still true?', and role prefixes like 'system:'. Write "The 2024 International Building Code is the current IBC edition.", not "Verify that the 2024 IBC is the current edition."

evidence_refs.description: 1-20 evidence references the conclusion relies on: plain http(s) URL strings, or { url, document_id } objects with unique document_id values

document_id.description: stable document identity, reusable for later change notifications

idempotency_key.description: reuse the operation key returned by an ambiguous prior attempt; omit for a new operation

name: verify
